## Basics of using git

Git is a distributed version control system (VCS) that is very popular

The core steps to using git involve

1. initiate a git repository (the tick box before we start a project in R studio)
    In RStudio we just click a little radio button on project creation
    At the command line we type: `git innit`
    
2. do your normal work
    add files 
    modify files etc.
    
3. add your important files to the "stage" 
    in RStudio we click "stage" radio button 
    `git add yourfilename`
    
    
4. commit your staged files to the repository 
    In RStudio you just hit the "Commit" button and add a msg 
    `git commit -m "your wee msg`
    
you can check your project "history" and status 
    `git status` 
    `git log` (push Q to exit)
    

## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this 

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
